blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane has proven itself in production: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (provider selected per environment), or at least keep the Stripe account open and the previous release deployable for a stated period (for example several weekly deploy cycles), and only close the account and delete the client in a later change. Failure scenario: Paylane rejects or times out on authorizations after the release; redeploying the previous version (blue/green) does not help once the Stripe account is closed the next day, so card payments stay down until a new release is built. State the rollback procedure and the condition for closing the Stripe account in the design, and add a task for the switch.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide how operators see the worker's health: a log at start and end of each run with structured fields (run date, payments fetched, matched, unmatched), a metric or a last-successful-run timestamp, and an alert when a run fails or does not complete by a deadline. Failure scenario: the Paylane API is unreachable at 02:00 or the CronJob is never scheduled; the job fails, nothing is written, and since the only alert in the plan fires on unmatched payments, the finance channel stays silent and the night's settlement is missing unnoticed — the requirement "Payments are settled nightly" is broken without a signal. Also say whether a failed run may be re-run safely for the same day (idempotent matching) and add the monitoring to task 1.2.
findings.title: The settlement worker can fail without anyone seeing it
